title: DfT / GOV.UK – Port & domestic waterborne freight stats (PORT tables; includes ship arrivals tables like PORT0601/0602)
period: Quarterly data available from 2009 to present (latest update covers up to September 2025).
brief_description: A comprehensive repository of statistical data tables from the UK Department for Transport. It details the international and domestic movement of freight by water, including total port traffic, cargo types, major routes, ship arrivals, and vessel flags.
highlighted_comment: This is a primary official source for UK maritime logistics.
notes: The data is provided in ODS format rather than standard Excel/CSV, which may require conversion for certain data pipelines.
dashboard_use: Road/rail access monitoring and disruption explanation

title: DfT – Maritime Statistics Dashboard (interactive maps & comparisons)
period: Annual data (visualizes trends over recent years).
brief_description: An interactive web-based dashboard and map that visualizes the movement of goods through UK ports. It illustrates global shipping routes, domestic traffic flows, and port-specific throughput volumes.
highlighted_comment: It is for Visualization Only. This tool is excellent for taking screenshots to visually represent trade routes or port density in your document, but it is not suitable for extracting raw data.
dashboard_use: Road/rail access monitoring and disruption explanation

category: Tides / sea level / coastal conditions / flood risk (environmental drivers)
title: Environment Agency – Flood-monitoring API reference (warnings, levels, flows, stations)
period: Real-time (updated every 15 minutes) with access to recent historical readings (typically rolling ~28 days via API).
brief_description: The official technical documentation for the UK Environment Agency's REST API. It allows developers to programmatically fetch real-time data on flood warnings, river levels, rainfall, and groundwater levels across England.
highlighted_comment: Technical/Developer Resource. This is the "raw feed" used to build automated risk models. It is powerful if you are building a dynamic system (e.g., "Alert port operators if river levels exceed X meters"), but it requires coding skills (Python/R) to use.
dashboard_use: Crisis trigger, weather window, flood-risk signal

category: Weather & severe weather warnings (crisis triggers + forecasting)
title: Met Office – Weather DataHub (observations/forecasts & API products entry)
format: API (JSON/XML), GRIB (Gridded Binary for models), GeoJSON.
cost: Freemium. (Basic access is free; high-resolution/high-frequency commercial data requires a paid subscription).
period: Extensive Historical archives (decades) + Real-time + Future forecasts.
brief_description: The official data portal for the UK’s National Weather Service. It provides developer access to weather observations, site-specific forecasts, global model data, and climate records.
highlighted_comment: The Gold Standard for Weather Data. This is the authoritative source for atmospheric conditions (wind speed, visibility, precipitation) that affect maritime operations. Essential for modelling weather-related port disruptions (e.g., determining when wind speeds force crane stoppages).
dashboard_use: Crisis trigger, weather window, flood-risk signal

category: Weather & severe weather warnings (crisis triggers + forecasting)
title: Met Office – NSWWS Public API (machine-readable severe weather warnings)
period: Real-time (Current active warnings) and Forecast (up to 7 days ahead).
brief_description: The technical documentation for the API that delivers the UK's official severe weather warnings. It allows systems to automatically retrieve current and future alerts (Yellow, Amber, Red) for hazards like wind, rain, snow, ice, and fog.
highlighted_comment: The "Trigger" for Disruption Models. This is the specific data source that defines official "extreme" conditions. Use this data to define the threshold for when a port should stop operations in your model (e.g., "If Wind Warning = Amber, reduce capacity by 50%").
dashboard_use: Crisis trigger, weather window, flood-risk signal
